 8th Pay Commission: AICPI-IW trends could push dearness allowance to 67% before 8th CPC report. Here's how
 Personal Finance News
 8th Pay Commission: AICPI-IW trends could push dearness allowance to 67% before 8th CPC report. Here's how
 By Upstox News Desk 4 min read | Updated on October 29, 2026, 17:07 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 In the lead up to the 8th Pay Commission recommendations, the staff bodies have been demanding the 8th CPC to recommend point-to-point dearness allowance.
 8th CPC is likely to submit its final report by May 2027. | Image: Shutterstock
 Dearness Allowance (DA) for central government employees has been raised from 60% of basic pay to 63% with effect from July 1, 2026. Based on the 7th CPC formula, inflation trends, and assuming that the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW) holds at its August level through December 2026, the DA figure could climb to 67% from January 1, 2027. That would be a four-percentage-point jump in DA, landing just around four months before the 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) submits its report.

 In May 2027, the 8th CPC will complete 18 months since its notification in November 2025. By May 2027, it is expected to submit its recommendations to the Central Government.
 The DA calculation formula has not changed since 2016. Here, two sets of months matter. The instalment already fixed at 63% is based on AICPI-IW data from July 2025 to June 2026.
 The next instalment will depend on the AICPI-IW data from January to December 2026. Till now, data for eight months till August are in. September's reading is not yet published. Assuming the August number holds in the remaining months, DA from January 1, 2027 works out to be 67%. The article below explains the calculation: 
 The formula used to calculate DA is:
 DA = [{(Average AICPI-IW of last 12 months x 2.88)−261.41}/261.41]×100-Existing DA(%) 
 The AICPI-IW data for the 12 months from January to December 2026 are (assuming August number repeats for September to December):
 Month (2026) CPI-IW (2016=100) 
 January 148.6 
 February 148.5 
 March 149.1 
 April 149.9 
 May 150.8 
 June 151.9 
 July 153.2 
 August 154.4 
 September (assumed) 154.4 
 October (assumed) 154.4 
 November (assumed) 154.4 
 December (assumed) 154.4 
 Average 152.0 
 The average AICPI-IW is 152 for the 12 months from January to December 2026. We can put this value in the formula to find the DA number applicable from January 2027:
 DA = [{(152 x 2.88)−261.41}/261.41]×100-Existing DA(%)
 Let's do this step by step:
 Step 1: 152×2.88=437.76
 Step 2: 437.76−261.41=176.35
 Step 3: 176.35/261.41 = 0.674607
 Step 4: 0.674607×100=67.46%
 Step 5: Subtract existing DA (63%) = 67.46−63=4.46%
 Based on average AICPI-IW of 152, the formula yields 4.46% DA. However, the government usually rounds off the DA to a lower number, which means a DA hike of at least 4%, taking the total from 63% to 67%. The timing of such a hike will be interesting to watch.
 The 8th CPC's 18-month deadline, set in the November 2025 notification, expires in May 2027, and its report is expected around May–June 2027. The 67% instalment would take effect around four months earlier, making it probably the last DA revision under the 7th CPC structure before the new pay structure arrives.
 Please note that 67% DA will be possible only if the index stays flat till December. A monthly rise of the kind seen through 2026 may even push the average, and the final rate, higher. However, a lower AICPI-IW over months can push the next DA hike lower.
 In the lead up to the 8th Pay Commission recommendations, the staff bodies have been demanding the 8th CPC to recommend point-to-point DA. For instance, the FNPO has asked that “Point-to-Point DA without rounding-off should be provided.” It has further proposed that “the 8th CPC may recommend merger of DA/DR with Basic Pay whenever it crosses 25%.”
 The Bharat Pensioners Samaj has also proposed “quarterly revision of DA/DR on the basis of the three-month average, with point-to-point compensation.”
 However, there is a final wrinkle. When the 8th CPC's structure takes effect, DA may reset to zero and the accumulated 67% could be folded into the new basic pay. So 67% is not a permanent floor but it could be the last reading of the 7th CPC.
